finding.claim: Admin authorization on the ban endpoint is bypassed. require_admin signals failure by raising werkzeug's Forbidden via abort(403). The surrounding `except Exception` catches it, logs a warning, and execution continues to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin user can ban arbitrary users.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the protected ban operation

trace.note: Route handler for ban, reachable by any request that has g.user
non-admin: not is_admin is true, so abort(403) is reached
only logs a warning, with no return or re-raise
do_ban(uid) executes regardless of the check result

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only guard and its result is neutralized by the broad except. There is no other decorator, before_request hook, or return in the handler. The sibling unban route calls require_admin without a try, so it is correctly protected. The log line also writes the user name, which is minor.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) is the only guard. It aborts with 403 rather than returning a bool. The call at admin.py:17 sits inside try/except Exception (16-19), which swallows the abort. There is no before_request hook, decorator, or return in the handler.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17 require_admin calls abort(403) for a non-admin, admin.py:18 `except Exception` catches it, admin.py:19 only logs, and admin.py:20 do_ban(uid) runs regardless, so any authenticated non-admin can ban users. The unban route at admin.py:26 has no try and is correctly protected.
